lines.s: 很多人以為台灣的夏天只是熱，其實最讓人受不了的是濕度。空氣中的水分多，汗流出來不容易乾，所以即使溫度並不太高，人也會覺得又熱又不舒服。

lines.en: Many think Taiwan's summer is just hot, but what's really unbearable is the humidity. With so much moisture in the air, sweat doesn't dry easily, so even when it isn't that hot, it feels muggy.

explain.zh: 「最讓人受不了的是濕度。空氣中的水分多」。
explain.en: "The humidity": lots of moisture in the air.

lines.en: Since Taiwan's high-speed rail opened in 2007, Taipei to Kaohsiung takes only about an hour and a half, greatly shrinking the distance between north and south. Many people changed how they live: some live in Taichung and commute to Taipei by high-speed rail every day; some companies have put offices near the stations. But tickets cost more than ordinary trains — a considerable expense for frequent travellers — so the operator offers discounts such as student fares and early-booking reductions. Meanwhile, domestic flights lost many passengers after it opened, and some routes have even stopped.

Calligraphy needs concentration; no stroke can be rushed, and many feel much calmer afterwards. Some parents have their children learn it too, hoping to build patience.

lines.en: Small as it is, Taiwan has over two hundred peaks above three thousand metres. Hiking has become very popular, and at weekends mountain trails are full of groups of hikers. But as numbers rise, so do accidents: some inexperienced people go up unprepared, and when the weather suddenly changes they easily get lost or hurt. To reduce accidents, the government offers hiking courses teaching map reading and how to handle emergencies. Experts also advise telling your family your route and taking enough water and food.

lines.en: In the past most young Taiwanese left for the big cities, leaving only the old and the very young in the countryside. In recent years, though, more and more young people have chosen to go home. Some take over their parents' fields and grow vegetables without pesticides using new methods; some turn old houses into guesthouses or cafés to attract visitors; others sell local specialities nationwide online. They have not only created jobs for themselves but brought quiet villages back to life. Starting a business back home isn't easy, though: lack of money and small markets are common problems.

lines.en: Under the pressure of online bookshops and e-books, many of Taiwan's physical bookshops closed. In recent years, though, small but distinctive "independent bookshops" have appeared everywhere. Their owners often have ideas of their own: some sell only travel books, some only children's picture books, and some hold regular reading groups and talks. They believe a bookshop is not just a place to sell books but a space where people meet. Running one is hard and doesn't pay much, but many readers make a point of supporting them, because there they find a warmth big chains lack.

lines.zh: 您做手語翻譯已經十多年了，當初為什麼會走上這條路？
lines.en: You've been a sign-language interpreter for over ten years. How did you come to it?

lines.s: 我的父母都是聽障者，從小我就用手語跟他們溝通。長大以後，我發現社會上很多場合都缺少手語翻譯，聽障朋友常常沒辦法得到完整的資訊，所以就決定把它當成工作。
lines.zh: 我的父母都是聽障者，從小我就用手語跟他們溝通。長大以後，我發現社會上很多場合都缺少手語翻譯，聽障朋友常常沒辦法得到完整的資訊，所以就決定把它當成工作。
lines.en: Both my parents are deaf, so I've signed with them since I was small. When I grew up I found many settings lacked interpreters and deaf people often couldn't get full information, so I made it my job.

lines.s: 手語翻譯最困難的地方是什麼？
lines.zh: 手語翻譯最困難的地方是什麼？
lines.en: What's hardest about interpreting?

lines.s: 是速度。說話的人講得很快，我必須馬上理解，再用手語表達出來，中間幾乎沒有思考的時間。而且中文有很多成語，要用手語表達清楚，非常不容易。
lines.zh: 是速度。說話的人講得很快，我必須馬上理解，再用手語表達出來，中間幾乎沒有思考的時間。而且中文有很多成語，要用手語表達清楚，非常不容易。
lines.en: Speed. Speakers talk fast and I have to understand at once and sign it, with almost no time to think. And Chinese has many set phrases that are very hard to sign clearly.

lines.s: 您覺得社會對聽障者的了解夠嗎？
lines.zh: 您覺得社會對聽障者的了解夠嗎？
lines.en: Do you think society understands deaf people well enough?

lines.s: 比以前進步多了。現在電視新聞和政府的記者會都有手語翻譯，但是在醫院、學校這些日常場合還是很缺乏。我希望有更多年輕人願意學手語，讓聽障朋友的生活更方便。
lines.zh: 比以前進步多了。現在電視新聞和政府的記者會都有手語翻譯，但是在醫院、學校這些日常場合還是很缺乏。我希望有更多年輕人願意學手語，讓聽障朋友的生活更方便。
lines.en: Much better than before. TV news and government press conferences now have interpreters, but everyday places like hospitals and schools still lack them. I hope more young people will learn sign language and make deaf people's lives easier.

lines.en: I always say a pet is a lifelong responsibility: don't buy one on a whim, and never abandon it because you move or marry. If you really want one, consider adopting first.

lines.zh: 這跟歷史有關。早在幾十年前，台灣的少年棒球隊就在國際比賽中拿到冠軍，那時候全國的人半夜爬起來看電視，棒球就成了大家共同的回憶。
lines.en: It's historical. Decades ago Taiwan's youth baseball teams won international championships; the whole country got up in the middle of the night to watch, and baseball became a shared memory.

lines.en: More play basketball now, but whenever there's an international game the stadium is packed. When Taiwan last won a world title, every street was celebrating.

lines.en: Skill matters, of course, but above all I want them to learn teamwork. Baseball isn't a one-person game; even the best pitcher needs teammates to win.

lines.en: Hello listeners. Today's topic is plant milk. More and more people drink oat milk, soy milk or almond milk instead of cow's milk — some because milk upsets their stomach, some for the environment, since cattle produce lots of greenhouse gases, and some simply prefer the taste. But nutritionists warn that plant milks may not match cow's milk for protein and calcium, so check the nutrition label and get them from other foods if needed.

lines.en: Anping in Tainan is one of the earliest-developed places in Taiwan. Four hundred years ago the Dutch built a fort here; later Koxinga drove them out and Anping became an important port. Walking its old street today you can still see ancient walls and temples and eat famous snacks like shrimp crackers and douhua. Many visitors watch the sunset by the sea in the evening. The local government has restored many old houses and encouraged young people to return and open shops, so the old street keeps its history while gaining new energy.

lines.en: Many think childhood is the best time to learn a language and that it's hard later. Research finds adults have their own advantages: stronger comprehension, quick mastery of grammar rules, and better systematic methods. Their real difficulty is usually not ability but lack of time and fear of mistakes. Experts suggest weaving learning into daily life — listening to foreign-language programmes on the commute, writing shopping lists in the language — a little every day works better than one long weekly class.

lines.en: I've been an A&E nurse at a hospital for ten years. The pace is very fast — often the next patient arrives before the last is dealt with. What upsets me most isn't the hard work but relatives who lose their temper after waiting long. I learned to explain the patient's situation first so families understand why they must wait, and most people accept it. The greatest reward is the 'thank you' from relatives when a patient recovers and goes home.

lines.en: You're one of Taiwan's few women fishing-boat captains. Why did you choose this work?

lines.s: 我家三代都是漁民，小時候常跟爸爸出海。大學畢業後我在台北上班，可是一直想念海的味道。爸爸生病以後，我就決定回來接手家裡的船。

lines.en: My family have been fishermen for three generations; as a child I often went to sea with my dad. After university I worked in Taipei but always missed the sea. When Dad fell ill, I decided to come back and take over the boat.

lines.en: Yes — many old fishermen didn't believe a woman could be captain, and some wouldn't sail with me. I could only prove myself by results: in the first year our catch was bigger than before, and gradually they accepted me.

lines.en: Ocean resources are shrinking; we can't just think of catching more fish. Now I take visitors to sea to experience fishing and teach them about marine ecology, hoping more people will help protect the ocean.

lines.en: You've studied Formosan black bears for twenty years. How are they doing?

lines.s: 野外的數量大概只有幾百隻，比以前少很多。主要的原因是棲息地被破壞，還有一些人在山上設陷阱抓其他動物，黑熊不小心被夾到。
lines.zh: 野外的數量大概只有幾百隻，比以前少很多。主要的原因是棲息地被破壞，還有一些人在山上設陷阱抓其他動物，黑熊不小心被夾到。
lines.en: There are only a few hundred in the wild, far fewer than before. The main causes are habitat destruction and traps set for other animals, which bears get caught in.

lines.zh: 我們跟山上的原住民部落合作，請他們不要設陷阱，並且一起巡山。部落的長輩對山林非常了解，常常比我們更早發現黑熊的蹤跡。
lines.en: We work with Indigenous mountain communities, asking them not to set traps and patrolling together. The elders know the forest very well and often spot signs of bears before we do.

lines.zh: 最簡單的是，去山上的時候不要亂丟食物，也不要餵野生動物。另外，買東西的時候可以選擇對環境友善的產品，支持保護山林的農民。
lines.en: The simplest thing is not to leave food lying around in the mountains or feed wild animals. And when shopping, choose eco-friendly products that support farmers who protect the forest.

There are sixteen officially recognised peoples, each with its own language, dress and ceremonies — the Amis harvest festival, for example, usually in summer, when the community dances for days to thank ancestors and nature. Recently many villages have developed cultural tourism with craft and cooking experiences. Some members worry too much tourism will drain the ceremonies of meaning, so some villages close certain rites to outsiders.

Experts say these measures raise staff satisfaction and reduce congestion and pollution — good for society as a whole.

lines.en: Many know the experience: you know you should revise, yet you keep scrolling or tidying and won't start. Psychologists call it procrastination. Research finds procrastinators aren't necessarily lazy; often they fear failure or feel the task is too big to know where to begin. Experts suggest breaking a big task into small steps — read ten pages, then rest — and rewarding yourself for each small goal. This lowers psychological pressure and makes it easier to keep going.

lines.en: I'm a coffee farmer and have grown coffee in Gukeng, Yunlin, for fifteen years. Many don't know Taiwan can grow good coffee. Gukeng's altitude and climate suit it, but plantations are small and labour costly, so it's much dearer than imports. At first I feared it wouldn't sell; then I opened the farm to visitors and taught them to pick and roast beans. Having done it themselves, many appreciate the work behind a cup and are keener to support local coffee.

lines.en: You run a second-hand furniture shop in Taipei. Why this trade?

lines.s: 我以前在搬家公司工作，常常看到很多人搬家時把還很好的家具丟掉，覺得非常可惜。所以我就開始把這些家具收回來，整理、修理以後再賣出去。
lines.zh: 我以前在搬家公司工作，常常看到很多人搬家時把還很好的家具丟掉，覺得非常可惜。所以我就開始把這些家具收回來，整理、修理以後再賣出去。
lines.en: I used to work for a removals firm and often saw people throw away perfectly good furniture when moving — such a waste. So I began taking it back, tidying and repairing it, and selling it on.

lines.s: 客人主要是哪些人？
lines.zh: 客人主要是哪些人？

lines.en: Many are young people just starting work, on tight budgets but not wanting cheap furniture that breaks quickly. Others love the feel of old pieces and come specially for vintage items.

lines.en: Space. Furniture takes up room and warehouse rent is high. Now we post photos online first and deliver from the warehouse once a customer decides, so the shop needs to hold less.

lines.s: 您在偏鄉當醫生已經二十年了，偏鄉的醫療最缺少什麼？
lines.zh: 您在偏鄉當醫生已經二十年了，偏鄉的醫療最缺少什麼？
lines.en: You've been a rural doctor for twenty years. What does rural healthcare lack most?

lines.s: 最缺的是人。年輕醫生大多想留在大城市，願意來偏鄉的很少。有時候整個鄉只有一位醫生，生病的老人要坐兩個小時的車才能到大醫院。
lines.zh: 最缺的是人。年輕醫生大多想留在大城市，願意來偏鄉的很少。有時候整個鄉只有一位醫生，生病的老人要坐兩個小時的車才能到大醫院。
lines.en: People, most of all. Young doctors mostly want to stay in cities; few will come to rural areas. Sometimes a whole township has one doctor, and sick elderly people must ride two hours to a big hospital.

lines.s: 那您們怎麼解決？
lines.zh: 那您們怎麼解決？
lines.en: How do you cope?

lines.s: 我們開始用遠距醫療，在診所透過視訊讓大醫院的專科醫生幫忙看病。另外，我們也培訓村裡的年輕人當照護員，定期去老人家裡量血壓、提醒吃藥。
lines.zh: 我們開始用遠距醫療，在診所透過視訊讓大醫院的專科醫生幫忙看病。另外，我們也培訓村裡的年輕人當照護員，定期去老人家裡量血壓、提醒吃藥。
lines.en: We've started telemedicine, letting specialists at big hospitals see patients by video from our clinic. We also train young villagers as carers who visit the elderly regularly to check blood pressure and remind them to take medicine.

lines.s: 您覺得這些方法有效嗎？
lines.zh: 您覺得這些方法有效嗎？
lines.en: Do these methods work?

lines.s: 很有幫助，但是不能完全取代醫生。我最希望的，是有更多年輕醫生願意來偏鄉看看，親身感受這裡的需要。
lines.zh: 很有幫助，但是不能完全取代醫生。我最希望的，是有更多年輕醫生願意來偏鄉看看，親身感受這裡的需要。
lines.en: They help a lot, but can't fully replace doctors. What I most hope is that more young doctors will come and see rural areas and feel the need here for themselves.

lines.en: Good evening and welcome to this week's travel show. We're in Chishang, Taitung, famous for its delicious rice. Each autumn, when the rice ripens, the fields turn golden and draw many people to cycle and take photos. Its best-known sight is a road with no power poles, rice fields on both sides — a wide-open view. Local farmers told us the rice is good because the water is clean and the days and nights differ greatly in temperature. If you like quiet country life, Chishang is well worth a visit.

lines.en: Many young people procrastinate: they know something needs doing but put it off to the last minute. A psychologist says procrastination isn't always laziness; sometimes it's fear of failure, or a task feeling too big to start. He suggests breaking big jobs into small steps and rewarding yourself after each one. Keeping your phone out of sight also reduces distraction. Most importantly, don't keep blaming yourself, as that only drains motivation.

lines.s: 台灣的珍珠奶茶已經紅到世界各地。它的起源有幾種說法，其中一種是在1980年代，台中一家茶館的店員把粉圓加進奶茶裡，沒想到大受歡迎。後來，珍珠奶茶從台灣傳到日本、美國和歐洲，成了台灣的代表飲料之一。現在的珍珠奶茶口味越來越多，除了傳統的紅茶，還有綠茶、烏龍茶，甚至加了水果。不過也有營養師提醒，一杯全糖的珍珠奶茶熱量很高，最好不要天天喝。
lines.zh: 台灣的珍珠奶茶已經紅到世界各地。它的起源有幾種說法，其中一種是在1980年代，台中一家茶館的店員把粉圓加進奶茶裡，沒想到大受歡迎。後來，珍珠奶茶從台灣傳到日本、美國和歐洲，成了台灣的代表飲料之一。現在的珍珠奶茶口味越來越多，除了傳統的紅茶，還有綠茶、烏龍茶，甚至加了水果。不過也有營養師提醒，一杯全糖的珍珠奶茶熱量很高，最好不要天天喝。
lines.en: Taiwan's bubble tea is popular worldwide. There are several stories of its origin; one says that in the 1980s a teahouse worker in Taichung added tapioca balls to milk tea, and it was a surprise hit. It spread to Japan, America and Europe, becoming one of Taiwan's signature drinks. There are now ever more flavours — besides black tea, green and oolong, even with fruit. Dieticians warn that a full-sugar cup is high in calories and shouldn't be an everyday drink.

lines.s: 很多人覺得學外語最難的是開口說話，因為怕說錯被別人笑。一位語言老師分享她的經驗：她剛到國外留學的時候，也很害怕說話，後來她發現，當地人其實很樂意幫助外國人，就算說錯也不會笑她。於是她每天強迫自己跟店員、鄰居聊天，三個月以後，她的口語進步了很多。她認為，學語言就像學游泳，光看書是學不會的，一定要下水才行。
lines.zh: 很多人覺得學外語最難的是開口說話，因為怕說錯被別人笑。一位語言老師分享她的經驗：她剛到國外留學的時候，也很害怕說話，後來她發現，當地人其實很樂意幫助外國人，就算說錯也不會笑她。於是她每天強迫自己跟店員、鄰居聊天，三個月以後，她的口語進步了很多。她認為，學語言就像學游泳，光看書是學不會的，一定要下水才行。
lines.en: Many find speaking the hardest part of learning a language, for fear of being laughed at. A language teacher shared her experience: when she first studied abroad she was scared to speak, then found locals were glad to help foreigners and didn't laugh at mistakes. So she made herself chat with shop staff and neighbours every day, and three months later her speaking had improved greatly. She thinks learning a language is like learning to swim: you can't learn from books — you have to get in the water.

lines.s: 您好，聽說您在花蓮開了一家民宿，為什麼會想做這個？
lines.zh: 您好，聽說您在花蓮開了一家民宿，為什麼會想做這個？
lines.en: Hello — I hear you run a B&B in Hualien. Why did you start it?

lines.s: 我以前在台北當工程師，工作壓力很大。有一次來花蓮旅行，覺得這裡的山和海太美了，就決定搬過來。
lines.zh: 我以前在台北當工程師，工作壓力很大。有一次來花蓮旅行，覺得這裡的山和海太美了，就決定搬過來。
lines.en: I used to be an engineer in Taipei, under a lot of pressure. On a trip to Hualien I found the mountains and sea so beautiful that I decided to move.

lines.s: 開民宿跟您想像的一樣嗎？
lines.zh: 開民宿跟您想像的一樣嗎？
lines.en: Is running a B&B as you imagined?

lines.s: 不太一樣。開民宿其實很忙，要打掃、做早餐、回覆客人的訊息，有時候比以前上班還累。
lines.zh: 不太一樣。開民宿其實很忙，要打掃、做早餐、回覆客人的訊息，有時候比以前上班還累。
lines.en: Not really. It's actually busy — cleaning, making breakfast, answering guests' messages — sometimes more tiring than my old job.

lines.s: 那您後悔嗎？
lines.zh: 那您後悔嗎？
lines.en: Do you regret it?

lines.s: 一點也不。雖然累，但是每天都能看到海，也能認識來自各地的客人，我覺得很值得。
lines.zh: 一點也不。雖然累，但是每天都能看到海，也能認識來自各地的客人，我覺得很值得。
lines.en: Not at all. It's tiring, but I see the sea every day and meet guests from everywhere — it's worth it.

lines.s: 陳醫師，最近很多人說自己睡不好，這是為什麼呢？
lines.zh: 陳醫師，最近很多人說自己睡不好，這是為什麼呢？
lines.en: Dr Chen, many people say they sleep badly lately. Why is that?

lines.s: 原因很多，最常見的是睡前用手機。手機的光會讓大腦以為還是白天，所以不容易睡著。
lines.zh: 原因很多，最常見的是睡前用手機。手機的光會讓大腦以為還是白天，所以不容易睡著。
lines.en: There are many reasons; the commonest is using phones before bed. The light makes the brain think it's still day, so it's hard to fall asleep.

lines.s: 那睡前多久不要用手機比較好？
lines.zh: 那睡前多久不要用手機比較好？
lines.en: How long before bed should we stop using phones?

lines.s: 最好睡前一個小時就不要用。可以改成看書或聽輕鬆的音樂。
lines.zh: 最好睡前一個小時就不要用。可以改成看書或聽輕鬆的音樂。
lines.en: Ideally an hour before. Read or listen to relaxing music instead.

lines.s: 如果還是睡不著呢？
lines.zh: 如果還是睡不著呢？
lines.en: And if you still can't sleep?

lines.s: 不要一直躺在床上，可以起來做點簡單的事，等想睡了再回床上。如果長期睡不好，就要來看醫生。
lines.zh: 不要一直躺在床上，可以起來做點簡單的事，等想睡了再回床上。如果長期睡不好，就要來看醫生。
lines.en: Don't keep lying there; get up and do something simple, and go back to bed when sleepy. If it lasts a long time, see a doctor.

q.zh: 醫生說睡不好最常見的原因是：

q.zh: 手機的光為什麼會影響睡眠？

q.zh: 醫生建議睡前多久不要用手機？

lines.s: 林先生，您的書店開了二十年，是這條街上最老的店。現在網路書店這麼方便，您怎麼經營下去？
lines.zh: 林先生，您的書店開了二十年，是這條街上最老的店。現在網路書店這麼方便，您怎麼經營下去？
lines.en: Mr Lin, your bookshop has been open twenty years, the oldest on this street. With online bookshops so convenient, how do you keep going?

lines.s: 一開始真的很辛苦，客人越來越少。後來我想，網路書店賣的是書，我能賣的是「經驗」。
lines.zh: 一開始真的很辛苦，客人越來越少。後來我想，網路書店賣的是書，我能賣的是「經驗」。
lines.en: It was really hard at first; customers kept falling. Then I thought: online shops sell books; what I can sell is experience.

lines.s: 什麼樣的經驗呢？
lines.zh: 什麼樣的經驗呢？
lines.en: What kind of experience?

lines.s: 我們每個月辦讀書會，請作家來跟讀者聊天，也幫客人推薦適合他們的書。很多客人說，來這裡就像來朋友家。
lines.zh: 我們每個月辦讀書會，請作家來跟讀者聊天，也幫客人推薦適合他們的書。很多客人說，來這裡就像來朋友家。
lines.en: We hold a reading group every month, invite authors to talk with readers, and recommend books to suit each customer. Many say coming here is like visiting a friend.

lines.s: 那現在的生意怎麼樣？
lines.zh: 那現在的生意怎麼樣？
lines.en: And how is business now?

lines.s: 比最困難的時候好多了，不少年輕人也會特地從外地來。
lines.zh: 比最困難的時候好多了，不少年輕人也會特地從外地來。
lines.en: Much better than at the worst, and many young people make a special trip from elsewhere.

q.zh: 這家書店開了多久？

q.zh: 林先生認為自己能賣的是：

q.zh: 現在書店的生意怎麼樣？
q.en: How is business now?

explain.zh: 「比最困難的時候好多了」。
